rules.statement: Implement each client authentication method as its own handler with its own descriptor; don't make one handler advertise several methods, even when they share a base class.
rules.why: Each method has to be advertised and registered on its own. If a deployment registers only one method, only that one should be advertised.
rules.check: Look for a client authentication handler whose descriptor covers more than one token_endpoint_auth_method, or that branches internally to serve both private_key_jwt and client_secret_jwt.

rules.statement: A JWT client assertion handler reads client_assertion and client_assertion_type only from a form POST body, and returns Undefined (defers) unless the type is exactly urn:ietf:params:oauth:client-assertion-type:jwt-bearer.
rules.why: Client authentication is a strategy collection: a handler that doesn't own the request must defer so a sibling can handle it.
rules.check: Check that the handler compares client_assertion_type to the jwt-bearer constant before doing anything else, returns Undefined otherwise, and doesn't read the assertion from the query string or headers.

rules.statement: A JWT client assertion handler claims an assertion only when its alg resolves to a signature algorithm of the handler's own key family: asymmetric for private_key_jwt, symmetric (HMAC) for client_secret_jwt. It leaves `none`, unknown algorithms and the other family's algorithms to the sibling handler.
rules.why: Each assertion should be handled exactly once. A handler that authenticates an algorithm from its sibling's family is called out as a smell.
rules.check: Check that the handler resolves alg through the algorithm collection, filters by the key family (for example AcceptsOnly<AsymmetricSecretKey>() or AcceptsOnly<SymmetricSecretKey>()), and defers rather than accepting `none` or a cross-family alg.

rules.statement: When authenticating a client from a JWT assertion, require iss and sub to both be present and equal, locate the client by sub, and don't require a separate client_id parameter.
rules.why: OpenID Connect Core §9 pins iss == sub == client_id, and FAPI private_key_jwt clients send only the assertion.
rules.check: Look for a missing iss/sub equality check, a lookup by iss alone, or code that rejects an assertion because no client_id form parameter was sent.

rules.statement: Verify a client assertion only after confirming the client is registered for the handler's authentication method, and only against the keys resolved for that client.
rules.why: A client may authenticate only with its registered method, and the assertion proves identity only through that client's own keys.
rules.check: Check that the signature is validated against the client's resolved key set (stored keys or jwks_uri), not a global key set, and that the client's registered auth method is checked.

rules.statement: Accept a client assertion's alg only if it is in the client's effective token_endpoint_auth_signing_alg_values_supported, narrowed to the single registered token_endpoint_auth_signing_alg when one is set. Treat an unset list as permitting nothing.
rules.why: JWTs exchanged with a client must follow its registered metadata within its effective ceilings.
rules.check: Look for alg validation that falls back to all supported algorithms when the client's list is empty, or that ignores a registered token_endpoint_auth_signing_alg.

rules.statement: Accept a client assertion audience only if it is the tenant's issuer or the receiving endpoint's URL built from the tenant's published origins, never from the request's Host. Apply any issuer-only restriction through a security profile requirement after validation, not as the default.
rules.why: Accepting the issuer or the endpoint URL works with both generic OpenID Connect and FAPI clients. URLs the server compares must not take their origin from the request's host.
rules.check: Look for audience comparisons against a URL derived from HttpRequest.Host, or a hard-coded issuer-only check outside the security profile mechanism.

rules.statement: When validating a client assertion, require exp, apply the client's effective clock skew, cap the lifetime at the configured maximum assertion lifetime, and refuse a key whose x5c certificate is outside its validity period.
rules.why: A client-signed JWT must be short-lived so that a captured one has a bounded window of use.
rules.check: Check for optional exp handling, a missing lifetime cap, a hard-coded skew instead of the client's effective clock_skew, or x5c certificates accepted without a validity check.

rules.statement: Make a client assertion single-use: require jti, and record it atomically, keyed by tenant, client_id and jti, in a shared-state expiring key set until exp plus the clock skew, so replay is detected on every replica.
rules.why: An assertion is a bearer credential. A replay cache held only in process lets a replica that didn't see the assertion accept it again.
rules.check: Look for a missing or optional jti, a check-then-add instead of an atomic add, a key that leaves out tenant or client_id, an in-memory-only cache, or an expiry shorter than exp plus skew.

rules.statement: Once a JWT client assertion handler has claimed an assertion, make every refusal a conclusive invalid_client error that the failed-authentication limiter counts; never defer after claiming.
rules.why: Refusals must be conclusive and rate-limited, so that a failed assertion can't fall through to another handler or escape the limiter.
rules.check: Look for validation failures after ownership that return Undefined, return an error code other than invalid_client, or skip the failed-authentication limiter.

rules.statement: Don't treat client_secret_jwt as FAPI-eligible: a FAPI security profile must allow only private_key_jwt or mutual TLS for client authentication.
rules.why: client_secret_jwt keys its HMAC from a reversible shared secret, which doesn't meet FAPI's requirement for strong client authentication.
rules.check: Look for FAPI profile configuration or eligibility checks that list client_secret_jwt or client_secret_basic/post as permitted.
